Each year, over 87 millions passengers arrive on flights in the Czech Republic to experience the wonders of this central European country, famed for its fine architecture, relaxed ambiance, and vibrant nightlife. Most travelers arrive at the Czech Republic's major airports, the busiest of which is Prague International, with over 17 million passengers passing through its polished corridors each year (as of 2018). Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic and the most popular destination for travelers, with many visitors from other European countries visiting as it is a popular destination for long-weekends. Another big airport is Brno, which serves the city of the same name that's famous for innovative modernist architecture and which attracts design buffs from all over the world. The other major airports in the Czech Republic are Ostrava, Karlovy and Pardubice​ airports, which serve the major tourist destinations of the Czech Republic. Both international and local airlines provide flights in the Czech Republic. Czech Airlines and Smartwings connect the Czech Republic's major cities with popular European and Asian capitals. United Airlines provides services to the Czech Republic from the United States, frequently in partnership with European partners for indirect flights. Flight companies in the Czech Republic Both national and international companies provide flights in the Czech Republic. The most famous Czech airlines are Czech Airlines, the flag-carrying airline in the country, and Smartwings. Czech Airlines flies to over 50 destinations worldwide, with routes to both European and Asian countries. Smartwings is a low-cost airline which predominantly flies to destinations across Europe, but also operates in Israel. Other Airlines which operate in the Czech Republic include Aegean Airlines, Air France, Alitalia, China Eastern, Eurowings, Fly Dubai, Ryanair, KLM, Luxair, Lufthansa, Swiss International, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines, Korean Air, easyJet, Turkish Airlines, United Airlines, vueling, and Volotea. Popular international routes by plane Flights in the Czech Republic typically depart from Prague, Brno, Ostrava, Karlovy and Pardubice​ airports. The busiest airport for flights in the Czech Republic is Prague international airport, which is where many national and international travelers to the country arrive from. A large volume of planes in the Czech Republic depart for Russia each day, and depart predominantly in the major cities of Moscow and St Petersburg. Scandinavia is a popular destination from the Czech Republic, with many flights arriving in Scandinavian capitals, including Finland's Helsinki, Norway's Oslo, and Sweden's Stockholm. In the United Kingdom, popular routes include flights departing to Prague from Birmingham International, Manchester Airport and London Gatwick, and a flight to Brno from Stansted.​ When arriving in the Czech Republic Travelers visiting the Czech Republic will be pleased to find a pleasant, modern and lively European country, with all available amenities. However, travelers should be conscientious of a few important things to bear in mind, before they enjoy their flights to the Czech Republic. Although the Czech Republic is part of the European Union, they do not use the Euro. If you have been traveling from other European countries to the Czech Republic, make sure to change your currency to Czech Crown​ in advance. Visitors to Prague will be pleased to note that many of the city's most popular tourist attractions are within walking distance from each other, and are frequently preferable to public transport, especially in the midst of summer. Remember to pack comfortable shoes in advance. However, public transport in the Czech Republic is clean, efficient and well-connected, making it frequently preferable to driving in a private car. Travelers will find intercity connections by bus and train very comfortable.
